note: Inputs for the deterministic bullwhip metrics in the oil and gas segment. Every series is labelled SOURCE, DEMODATA or ASSUMPTION. The engine computes the metric values; nothing here is a result. Same method names and structure as the other segment's file.

metrics.name: Order amplification ratio
metrics.definition: (1 + growth of intermediary orders) / (1 + growth of end demand) over the same 12 months. Above 1.3 means intermediaries are ordering faster than end demand grows: amplification.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] intermediary orders = relay orders from engineering firms and switchgear builders for oil and gas projects; end demand = project spending that needs relays. Replace with ABB order intake by customer type and an operator capex series.

sources.name: Method: Lee, Padmanabhan, Whang (1997) bullwhip definition; ABB order intake (internal, not connected)

metrics.name: Brent price momentum (urgency-buying proxy)
metrics.definition: Change in the quarter-on-quarter price move. Prices rising but the move shrinking two quarters in a row is the pre-peak pattern; buyers in oil and gas also rush orders when the oil price jumps.
metrics.inputs_note: Quarter-on-quarter percentage change in the Brent spot quarterly average, computed from EIA STEO October 2026 Table 2: 2Q25 68.01, 3Q25 69.00, 4Q25 63.63, 1Q26 81.11, 2Q26 102.93, 3Q26 95.95 USD per barrel [SOURCE]. 4Q26 (forecast 104.69) is left out because it is a forecast. The use of the oil price as a proxy for urgency buying of relays is an ASSUMPTION.

sources.name: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026, Table 2 (Brent spot price, quarterly averages)

metrics.name: Double-ordering index (lead time vs distributor inventory)
metrics.definition: Lead times and distributor inventory days rising together means buyers are ordering ahead of need (hoarding). Lead times rising while inventory falls means genuine scarcity.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] changes over 12 months for industrial protection-relay parts. Replace with supplier lead-time quotes and distributor stock reports.

sources.name: Distributor stock reports and supplier quotes (not connected)

metrics.name: Distributor spot premium for relay parts
metrics.definition: Spot premium over contract price at distributors. A high premium means urgency; a collapsing premium while lead times are still long means hoarding is ending.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] entire series illustrative. Replace with distributor price lists against contract prices for the parts used in oil and gas relays.

metrics.name: Order push-out and cancellation rate (ABB internal)
metrics.definition: Share of frame-order quantities rescheduled out or cancelled in the last 90 days. The earliest internal sign that intermediaries over-ordered.
metrics.inputs_note: [ASSUMPTION] Not connected, no values given. Requires ABB SAP sales order change history (VBAP/VBEP schedule line changes), filtered to oil and gas customers.

analog_2021_2023.label: SOURCE+DEMODATA
analog_2021_2023.note: Shared with the other segment's file, because the electronic parts in protection relays went through the same cycle. Indexed shape of the 2021-2023 semiconductor cycle for visual comparison only. Anchors: Broadcom lead time 12.2 weeks (Feb 2020) to 22.2 weeks (Apr 2021); SIA 2022 sales USD 573.5 bn with December 2022 down 4.4% MoM; memory corrected first in 2022 and rebounded first in 2023. Intermediate points are illustrative.

sources.name: Wikipedia: 2020-2023 global chip shortage (lead time anchors)
Nomad Semi: State of the Semiconductor Cycle (SIA data)
Roland Berger: Semiconductor shortage, a different kind of (Oct 2022)
